Toolchain Components

This page lists the executables, plugin directories, and standard libraries in the SA / SLA toolchain one by one, with one sentence on each entry's role. After reading it you will know which command or which repository to look for for a given task.

Core Executables

NameSourceRole
sa.exesciThe SA host CLI: subcommands such as run / build / build-exe / build-wasm / test / plugin, loading and dispatching all plugins
sla.exesa_plugin_slaThe top-level sla command: shipped with the fully automatic installation bundle, or copied by the installation script into SCI\current\bin (the same directory as sa.exe, and likewise on PATH); functionally fully equivalent to sa sla …
Dynamic library (libsla.so / DLL) + sap.jsonsa_plugin_slaThe SLA compiler plugin itself, registered into the SA environment by sa plugin install --dev

Commands Provided by the SLA Plugin

The table below is written in terms of the top-level sla command; every form has an equivalent sa sla … form (drop the prefix to convert between them), as detailed in the Command-Line Reference chapter.

CommandPurpose
sla init [path]Create the skeleton of a minimal SLA binary project
sla check <file>Lexical, syntax, and type checking, without emitting final SA assembly
sla build <file>Compile a .sla file into a verified .sa assembly file
sla build-exe <file>Compile to a native executable; by default it takes the SA text path, and the SAB path requires an explicit --test-backend sab
sla sab build / sab workspace / sab disasmSAB compilation / compilation by workspace member / disassembly debugging; short alias slab
sla test <file>Compile, then run via sa test; the default auto backend lands on the SA text path, and SAB requires an explicit --test-backend sab
sla skills [--json]List the SLA plugin's capabilities; in text mode it also writes skill files into the current directory

Application Plugins at a Glance

Each plugin is a standalone project (its own sap.json + .sai/.sal + dynamic library) and can be installed and upgraded independently. The role descriptions come from the sci README:

Plugin directoryRole in one sentence
sa_plugin_saxThe SA UI dialect: .sax → app.wasm + airlock.js + index.html
sa_plugin_reactReact-on-SAX: write SA components with the React mental model
sa_plugin_muiMaterial UI components (early)
sa_plugin_viteDev server and .sax hot reload (Phase 2)
sa_plugin_wgpuBrowser WebGPU sidecar
sa_plugin_3dengines3D engine stack (aligned with Bevy)
sa_plugin_http_serverHTTP server
sa_plugin_http_clientHTTP client
sa_plugin_dbNative columnar database (file-backed)
sa_plugin_dbnetDatabase network layer
sa_plugin_matmulPhysical-limit GEMM matrix multiplication
sa_plugin_vmStandalone dynamic VM interpreter
sa_plugin_pkgZero-trust package management: URLs as namespaces, SHA-256 version locking, no central registry, module-level grants sandbox
sa_plugin_tuiTerminal capability ABI: ownership, size, output, mode switching, byte input events
sa_plugin_tsTypeScript → SA frontend
sa_plugin_denoDeno API subset frontend (experimental, not a Deno runtime)
sa_plugin_nodeNode API surface frontend (experimental, no V8/VM)
sa_plugin_bc2saclang/rustc → LLVM bitcode → SA (experimental)

TS Frontends: sa_plugin_ts and tsgo-sa (satsgo)

There are two TypeScript → SA frontends in the repositories: sa_plugin_ts (hand-written lexing/parsing, an explicit subset, all 286 demos passing sa check) and tsgo-sa (satsgo, reusing the production-grade TS parser/binder/checker, aiming to replace the former). Their shared discipline: reject loudly — anything outside the subset is reported with a located error, never silently mistranslated; the standard library uniformly reuses sci/sa_std or plugin-native backends, and the frontend does zero runtime emulation (machine-enforced by tools/check_sa_std_projection.sh).

  • Multi-file linking (tsgo-sa build): the import graph + reachable set; value cycles are rejected with the chain given; import type edges and value import edges "used only in type positions" are automatically erased; namespace objects such as export default {..} / export default ns reach member definitions directly (including destructuring like const {a, b: c} = NS); package.json dependencies are recorded in sa.mod comments and reports (require lines need a sha256; without a hash no valid line is output).
  • Type-driven layout: struct layouts prefer the record table, and when missing consult the checker (inferred types such as factory returns, anonymous-shaped field sets); type X = {..} aliases build layouts, and nested chains sink by field offset; class static literals are folded (heritage classes also publish statics; instantiation is still rejected); accessors (getter/setter) are only recorded, not inlined, and reads/writes report a dedicated diagnostic.
  • Guards and narrowing: ?. adds a join according to nullability; typeof v === "undefined" lowers to a null check (in the subset, null/undefined are unified as 0); Date narrows to i64 milliseconds (UTC), and now/getTime/toISOString/parse/get-family/setter/toString-family/valueOf project onto sa_std/time.sai (see the standard library time page). Arrow-function captures go through a shared use-name analysis (type names do not enter captures); the "unknown global" determination for unknown names in typeof goes through binder visibility (self-built scopes still govern ownership; the binder only answers visibility); typeof v === "undefined" lowers to a null check; generics are laid out monomorphized by actual argument (Box<i32> and Box<string> have different widths, and recursion converges through instance shells); typeof of a known type folds to a constant (folds only when a union agrees; any is still rejected). Note the NoLib decay: dialect primitive attributes (i32/u64 etc.) are Any in the checker's eyes, and type precision is effective only for real TS types (number/string/ interfaces/imported names); when writing portable TS, prefer real types.
  • Node/Deno projection: os/path/crypto/Hash/url/querystring/util/console/Buffer and Deno.* project by call shape onto native symbols in node.sai / deno.sai (u32 status checks, panic on nonzero; a missing Deno.env.get maps to null); Deno.env.* goes through two-level namespace routing; async (timers etc.) and missing pieces remain loud rejections. The complete surface is in section nine of the "node" page in the Plugin Reference.
  • TSX: static templates emit .sax directly; useState goes into state slots, and mount-time useEffect (empty bodies / setter constants) goes into @onMount; document.createElement/appendChild/setAttribute, createTextNode, textContent/innerHTML reads and writes, and el.textContent reads (caller scratch + panic on a full buffer), getAttribute/removeAttribute, and the className/id sugar reads project onto airlock DOM externs; console calls inside useEffect remain rejected (.sax has no print mechanism); all other hooks/dynamic forms are loudly rejected.
  • The loud-rejection register: async timers (6 of them, including setTimeout; no event loop, Phase 2), toLocale* (no locale backend), non-ISO Date.parse (panic, not NaN), dynamic Buffer.concat arrays, and format/inspect (no encoder/type guards). A user definition of the same name always takes priority over these rejections (the shadowing rule).

TS Frontend: tsgosa (a Thin typescript-go Port, State as of 2026-10)

tsgosa is a shallow clone of typescript-go: it reuses its production-grade parser/binder/checker, and at the end of the existing pipeline replaces JS emission with SA (a TranspileSA single-file port + the tsgo build program-chain interface), outputting .sai for consumption by sci/sa. Discipline: six iron rules (do it with the existing architecture, replace the JS logic, zero new Go files, no original semantics, main.go keeps only thin dispatch, and domain lowering lands in sa_*.go by ownership); reject loudly, and the standard library maps only to ready stock in sci/sa_std.

  • Progress (2026-10-12): 2146 examples in demos/, --check 2146/2146 + --corpus (286 agree against upstream) + native LLVM runs 2146/2146, all green. Coverage: pure computation/strings/the whole array family (including nested destructuring with defaults constructed on the spot for OOB: i32/string/nested elements; Array.of indexing/length; fresh-construction round trips; string-array OOB nullish fallback; compound assignment to string elements; array and object rest destructuring) / Map/Set/classes (including constructor wiring: nested-chain reads/string and array ?. guarded reads/this reads/compound assignment; full coverage of parameter positions) / i32 value-position handle defenses (arrays/strings/instances) / the boolean equality core (two booleans/mixed integer·call/subscript/Map-read loose equality) / interface layouts/all destructuring forms/the regex subset/Math/Date/the JSON subset/top-level snapshots (arrays/objects/template strings) / IIFE/tagged templates, etc.; the Node/Deno/http plugin surfaces are connected through the --dev chain.
  • Toolchain: Go 1.27 (/usr/local/go) + real Zig 0.17.0 (/opt/zig, first on PATH; the shim version is unusable) + llvm-14-dev (sci built with zig build -Dllvm=true, with a /content/sci symlink for plugin builds). "?", reusing the nullish core and guard slots, demos 1948–1957) and array defaults constructed on the spot for OOB (const [x = [9]] = nn, a new guard helper, demos 1958–1967) and array ?. subscript wiring (this.n = a?.[0] ?? -1, reusing the optional-subscript guard, demos 1968–1977, with the old 1954 lock removed) and wired this reads (this.n = this.n + k, the finit gate + thisSelf injection, demos 1978–1987) and wired compound assignment (this.n += k, delegating to the instance-field compound arm, demos 1988–1997) and i32 value-position handle defenses (array handles barred from entry, bare generics exempted, demos 1998–1999) and default sub-ownership (releases in reverse order inside the arm; string/nested defaults fully correct on real machines, 1966–1967 promoted, demos 2000–2001) and the boolean equality core (equality comparison of two boolean values, demos 2002–2011, with the old 1843 lock removed) and mixed boolean equality (loose equality on the integer side, demos 2012–2021) and the mixed call side (number/boolean-returning calls, demos 2022–2030) and the mixed subscript side (out-of-bounds folds to a value, demos 2031–2040) and mixed Map reads (a missing key folds to a value, demos 2041–2050) and the scattered-residue regression lock (demos 2051–2058, zero code changes) and the string-array OOB nullish lock (demos 2059–2065, zero code changes) and the parameter-position regression lock (demos 2066–2073, zero code changes) and compound assignment to string elements (demos 2074–2083) and array rest destructuring (demos 2084–2093) and object rest destructuring (a synthesized sub-layout for the rest domain + per-domain copying, demos 2094–2103, with the old 2093 rejection lock removed) and the rest-adjacent-forms lock warehouse (chained/function-object parameters/write-back/in folding + four rejections, demos 2104–2111, zero code changes) and the rest cross lock warehouse (spread backfill/JSON/class instances/optional domains/nesting + three rejections, demos 2112–2119, zero code changes) and the rest deep-edge lock warehouse (defaults/double spread/conditionals/f64/array push/inheritance/templates + one rejection, demos 2120–2127, zero code changes) and the rest statement lock warehouse (Map/for/switch/array construction/double rest/three-level nesting/while/call sources, demos 2128–2135, zero code changes) and the rest control-flow lock warehouse (nullish/this/try/do-while/string concatenation/branch functions/ternary values + one rejection, demos 2136–2143, zero code changes) and the TALG project proposal (top priority: full support for TheAlgorithms-TypeScript; Agent-First Host Commands

sci designs a set of self-explanatory commands for Agents: a global --json flag outputting structured diagnostics (stable error codes such as SA-REF-010, with repair suggestions), the compile_tokens / instruction_count metrics, and subcommands such as explain <code>, fix --plan --json, and skills. skills aggregates the syntax, macros, and API contracts of the currently enabled plugins, and in text mode refreshes the .codex/skills/… and .claude/skills/… files; before using it you should still confirm via sa plugin list or sa skills --json that the plugins are enabled.

Where sa_std Lives

The standard library is released with the sci repository, located at <sci 根目录>/sa_std/, containing .sa implementations, .sai interface contracts, and .sal macros, organized into per-module subdirectories (io, collections, mem, sync, text, os, etc.). SLA references it directly through @import "sa_std/…". Prebuilt artifacts are also available at artifacts/sa_std/libsa_std.a. Resolution order: the environment variable SA_STD_DIR takes priority; otherwise it falls back to $HOME/projects/sci/sa_std.

For the complete parameter documentation of each plugin command, see the Command-Line Reference chapter.
